ideas.name: Resonant Name-Songs
ideas.description: Sustained fundamental; upper harmonics move in small deliberate patterns; long vowels; sparse plucks.
ideas.verdict: Finalist 1. Strongest timbral signature.

ideas.name: Seven-Step Oath-Songs
ideas.description: Seven equal pulses grouped 2+2+3; syllabic calls; hard rests; low dry lute strokes.
ideas.verdict: Finalist 2. Best across all instrument families.

ideas.name: Close-Circle Songs
ideas.description: A lead syllabic line against two or three compact chordal response parts; rough bass timbre; synchronized releases.
ideas.verdict: Finalist 3. Strong ensemble reward, honest solo limitation.

ideas.name: Road-Debt Epics
ideas.description: Long prose-like verse on a two-note reciting formula; freely timed pauses; returning plucked refrain.
ideas.verdict: Reserve. Too close to Eastmarch declamation without a new timbral feature.

ideas.name: Contest of Names
ideas.description: Two alternating soloists progressively compress verses and shorten rests; repeating lute figure.
ideas.verdict: Reserve social form. Requires two visible singers and overlaps improvised bard contests elsewhere.

ideas.name: Forge Counts
ideas.description: A recurring pattern of three attacks and one silent slot; changing accents over a stable beat; clipped words.
ideas.verdict: Reserve occasion. Do not generate actual anvils or hammer sounds without visible sources. Too close to generic work music as a culture core.

ideas.name: Descending Stone Laments
ideas.description: Falling fourths; a held final low note; long unmetered phrases with minimal accompaniment.
ideas.verdict: Reject as core: Breton folk, Dunmer and Falkreath already occupy this space.

ideas.name: Ridge Calls
ideas.description: Wide vocal leaps with audible chest/head-register changes; answering flute figures and spacious pauses.
ideas.verdict: Strong alternate, particularly if Bosmer avoids register-break calls. Could become a northern vocal signature instead.

ideas.name: Knot Dances
ideas.description: Uneven five-pulse phrases, short repeated motifs, sharply articulated lute melody, abrupt cadences.
ideas.verdict: Reserve. Seven-Step offers a clearer single rhythmic fingerprint; do not proliferate adjacent odd meters immediately.

ideas.name: Embersong
ideas.description: Whispered or murmured narrow melody over very quiet lute pulses; long suspensions.
ideas.verdict: Reserve intimate mode. Too near Hjaalmarch hush and winterhold sparsity as a core.

ideas.name: Returning Ancestors
ideas.description: A refrain accumulates one new note each verse, then collapses to its original cell; alternating high/low lute registers.
ideas.verdict: Interesting formal variant, but cumulative form is unlikely to be recognized quickly in generated clips.

ideas.name: Burden-and-Release
ideas.description: Two increasingly dense phrases followed by a bar of silence; heavy/quiet dynamic contrast; three-note melody.
ideas.verdict: Reserve. Useful arrangement device inside Seven-Step rather than a separate tradition.

ideas.name: Resting Herd Songs
ideas.description: Long, unhurried pentatonic melody; sustained vowels; soft rocking accompaniment.
ideas.verdict: Reject as core: overlaps Khajiit drone and northern open-ended vocal styles.

ideas.name: Soot-Black Virtuosity
ideas.description: Fast repeated-note plucking, tight cross-string figures, abrupt switches of register, dry close sound.
ideas.verdict: Strong instrumental alternate. Risks merging with Redguard plucked virtuosity unless ornament and meter stay rigorously different.

ideas.name: Witness Recitation
ideas.description: Spoken rhythmic testimony gradually turns to one sustained sung pitch; single-string answers.
ideas.verdict: Reserve special occasion. Distinct form, but music generation and SkyrimNet spoken delivery may not align.

ideas.name: Long-Breath Flute
ideas.description: Low breathy tone alternates with clear higher harmonics; slow pitch changes over one repeated finger pattern.
ideas.verdict: Companion to Resonant Name-Songs, not independent core; avoid asking a normal single flute to supply an extra bass part.

ideas.name: Shieldless Boasts
ideas.description: Brisk syllabic verses, broad upward fourths, a snapped final syllable, plain diatonic melody.
ideas.verdict: Reserve lighter mode. Too near Nord tavern song to define the palette.

ideas.name: Broken-Line Canon
ideas.description: Three staggered entries repeat short lines at different phrase lengths; clashes resolve together every several cycles.
ideas.verdict: Reject as core: collides with Argonian interlocking and Hjaalmarch canon; ensemble requirement also high.

ideas.name: Leaping tales
ideas.description: Historical initial proposal: Springing seven-unit pulse grouped 2+2+3; short melody leaps a fourth or sixth, then stops; dry plucks; quick syllabic delivery. Current audition correction: five pulses grouped 3+2 replace the original seven pulses; use the current finalist fragments.
ideas.mood: Mischievous, poised, alert. A compelling ordinary Bosmer song grammar.
ideas.verdict: Finalist; first candidate to audition. Original 'default' wording is historical; the production core remains unset. Current meter: 3+2.

ideas.name: Hunting-call airs
ideas.description: Two- or three-note calls separated by complete silence; high and middle registers answer in sequence; clear tone and a clipped ending.
ideas.verdict: Finalist.

ideas.name: Spinner's tales
ideas.description: Speech follows a recurring three-note figure; each return adds or removes a beat; abrupt changes of register distinguish narrative turns.
ideas.verdict: Finalist.

ideas.name: Feast steps
ideas.description: Lively 3+3+2 pulse, open plucked intervals, a small refrain, sharply punctuated endings.
ideas.verdict: Reserve: reliable but less singular than #1; can collapse into familiar tavern dance.

ideas.name: Canopy exchanges
ideas.description: Two voices pass individual notes or syllables back and forth, assembling one agile line.
ideas.verdict: Ensemble reserve: distinguish with gaps and exchanged phrases, but too close to Argonian interlocking if made a core.

ideas.name: Register games
ideas.description: One singer switches chest and head register on wide leaps; sparse plucks mark only the low notes.
ideas.verdict: Technique reserve: strong sound, but a reference label such as yodel may dominate the worldbuilding or produce Alpine pastiche.

ideas.name: Quiet bow songs
ideas.description: Repeated low pluck answered by a high harmonic; spare three-note melody with long decays.
ideas.verdict: Reserve: good solo string piece, weaker group identity; risks merging with northern austerity.

ideas.name: Thorn dances
ideas.description: Fast five-unit pulse; tight ornaments, abruptly cut notes, sudden whole-beat rests.
ideas.verdict: Reserve alternate to #1; do not launch both before testing their audible separation.

ideas.name: Root cradle songs
ideas.description: Soft rocking duple motion; descending thirds, limited range, warm unadorned voice.
ideas.verdict: Later nuance: broadly plausible but does not solve the distinctness problem first.

ideas.name: Rain patterns
ideas.description: Repeated five-note cells, overlapping high and low figures, continuous regular pulse.
ideas.verdict: Reject as Bosmer default: already belongs to the Argonian design territory.

ideas.name: The long listening
ideas.description: Unmetered breathy flute, narrow register, long silence and almost no cadence.
ideas.verdict: Reject as default: too close to the Pale/Winterhold and Dunmer flute treatments. #2 uses precise calls and register contrast instead.

ideas.name: Boasting contests
ideas.description: A singer delivers a rhythmically crowded line followed by an intentionally tiny instrumental answer; each verse lengthens.
ideas.verdict: Strong later occasion; #1 can contain it without a separate core.

ideas.name: Knot refrains
ideas.description: A short melody gains a note or rhythm on each return, finally unravelling back to the original.
ideas.verdict: Reserve composition form: distinctive on paper; a generative model may not obey the cumulative rule audibly.

ideas.name: Hunting procession
ideas.description: Slow dotted five-beat tread; narrow, firmly projected chant; flute or string answers land on the same pitch.
ideas.verdict: Reject as default: overlaps Orc collective pulse and Nord declamation.

ideas.name: Shadow mourning
ideas.description: Widely spaced plucks interrupt a melody at uncomfortable places; words end before expected resolutions.
ideas.verdict: Later minority register: viable and distinctive by phrasing, but the existing palette already has many laments.

ideas.name: Court mimicry
ideas.description: An elegant symmetrical air repeatedly sprouts an extra beat, a register jump or an unexpected stop.
ideas.verdict: Traveling/individual repertoire: relies on knowing the court style being subverted.

ideas.name: Shared breath
ideas.description: Two flutes dovetail long tones, each enters as the other stops, producing one uninterrupted line.
ideas.verdict: Ensemble reserve: animation and breath staging difficult; the result erases our useful crisp/gapped fingerprint.

ideas.name: Skin and syllables
ideas.description: One performer alternates consonant-rich short sung phrases and muted finger taps in irregular groups.
ideas.verdict: Drum/voice branch of #3, not a fourth core.

ideas.name: Night harmonics
ideas.description: Sparse high flute overtones or plucked harmonics arranged in disjunct little constellations.
ideas.verdict: Instrumental reserve: can support #2; risk of generic magical ambience if heavily reverberant.

ideas.name: Returning story
ideas.description: Melody and rhythm reverse order halfway through, making a narrative circle with an exact final return.
ideas.verdict: Reject initial implementation: fragile prompt compliance; formal complexity may sound like Altmer cleverness.

ideas.name: Bough rustle
ideas.description: Rapid tremolo fades into soft repeated notes and returns in waves.
ideas.verdict: Reject as identity: generic texture and possible Khajiit/Redguard string overlap; also tempts the model to add environmental sound.

ideas.name: Animal portraits
ideas.description: A human voice uses distinct contours, articulation and registers to characterize animals in a tale.
ideas.verdict: Later narrator skill: musical characterization, not literal animal recordings or a claim about magical shapechanging.

boundaries.boundary: Articulated repeated cycles and firm returns / sustained slides and gradually unfolding development
boundaries.reserve: A separately researched Redguard narrative-ostinato branch, including possible griot influences

boundaries.boundary: Long melisma and modal tension / syllabic text-led stanzas / short descending five-beat cells
Rhetorical solo melody and harmonic arrivals / restrained intimacy / clear triple dance motion
boundaries.reserve: Distinct local vernaculars, not a universal College override

boundaries.boundary: Crisp continuous recurring cells / slow sustained adjacent-tone friction
boundaries.reserve: More varied communal Argonian responses after the core is audible

boundaries.boundary: Sparse circular vocables / long complete calls over slow rocking time
boundaries.reserve: A separately developed Skaal mode later

boundaries.boundary: Held resonance or synchronized firm attacks / quick changing phrases, leaps and gaps
boundaries.reserve: Further social occasions only after the main audition distinguishes them

boundaries.boundary: Independent moving/imitating lines / compact chord blocks that move and stop together
boundaries.reserve: Additional ensemble forms require their own visible roster
